title: Introduce latency-tier sparing, SLO-heatmap failover guardrail, and emergency route pinning hotpatch
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: recent incident (SUP-4319) showed cascading regional failovers when cold KV/evacuation events coincided with a tenant surge. The existing circuit logic aggressively reopens routes and triggers broad evacuations; this PR introduces three coordinated mitigations: 1) a low-latency-tier sparing path that proactively routes low-priority traffic to a soft slowpath under degraded capacity, preserving high-tier SLOs; 2) an SLO-Heatmap aggregator (per-region, per-tenant 1m buckets) used as a real-time guardrail to prevent aggressive failover decisions when the heatmap shows concentrated, transient pressure; 3) an emergency route pinning mechanism that pins traffic to a chosen compatible route for a short, configurable window during failover to avoid rapid reopen oscillations. This change is implemented behind a feature flag (slo_sparing.enabled=false by default) and has a staged rollout plan.

What this PR changes (high level): adds a heatmap aggregator service and API, integrates heatmap checks into the SLO decision path, introduces a latency-tier label and a soft slowpath admission controller, emergency_pin middleware in the router to pin routes for pin_duration (default 10s), and safety caps on simultaneous evacuations to prevent stampedes. Also includes telemetry dashboard JSON and a small CLI tool to inspect heatmap buckets.

Checklist:
- [x] heatmap aggregator implementation and persisted 1m sliding window
- [x] router emergency_pin middleware with pin_duration config
- [x] admission controller for latency-tier sparing + feature flag
- [x] telemetry emits: slo_heatmap.{region}.{tenant}.{bucket} and sparing_decision events
- [x] unit + integration tests updated
- [x] perf lab soak and canary rollout verified (see testing notes)
- [x] rollout/rollback plan documented

Testing & validation: unit tests cover aggregator boundaries, pin/unpin race windows, and admission controller decisions; integration tests run a simulated tenant surge to verify high-tier traffic keeps latency within SLA while low-tier traffic moves to slowpath. Perf-lab soak (12h) with injected KV pressure showed ~32% fewer evacuations during peak and stabilized reopen oscillations. Canary in us-west-2 for 2 hours (0.5% traffic) showed expected telemetry and no customer-facing errors. Integration test flake was observed once (integration suite timed out NVMe mock) and rerun on CI.

Rollout plan: feature flag disabled by default. Step 1: enable in perf and staging. Step 2: enable for 0.5% canary region traffic. Step 3: monitor slo_heatmap and eviction metrics for 4h thresholds before expanding. Rollback: flip slo_sparing.enabled=false; emergency_pin has a force-unpin admin endpoint for immediate rollback.

Related: ENG-9542 design doc (link in Linear), incident SUP-4319, SRE runbook updated.

review_comments: Evan Liu: Please emit a metric for 'sparing_decision' with reason tags (evacuation_avoid|kv_pressure|latency_spike). We need that to build alerts. Also add a short TTL for heatmap buckets so memory doesn't blow up.

Maya Patel: Default set to 10s and hardmax 60s enforced. Added e2e verifying force-unpin. Thanks!
Oliver Chen (SRE): Integration runs show evacuation cap prevented the stampede; please add a log line at INFO when cap is hit so we can correlate with incidents.
Maya Patel: Added info log and correlating trace id in sparing flow. Tests updated.

release_notes: hotfix: introduce optional latency-tier sparing and SLO heatmap guardrail. Default off; opt-in for canary. Helps prevent cascading evacuations during transient KV/latency pressure. Admins can force-unpin routes for immediate rollback.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: slo_sparing.enabled=false by default. Config knobs: slo_sparing.threshold (0-1), slo_heatmap.bucket_ms=60000, emergency_pin.pin_duration_default=10000ms, evac.cap_simultaneous=6. Watch metrics: slo_heatmap.*, sparing_decision.count, evacuation.count, emergency_pin.events. Dashboard added: observability/dashboards/slo-heatmap.json.
postmerge_actions: 1) Enable feature flag in perf, 2) run heatmap backfill tool for 1h to populate buckets (optional), 3) monitor SLO dashboards for 4h, 4) roll forward to canary if stable.
estimated_risk: medium (safety caps and feature flag reduce blast radius). New telemetry reduces unknowns; emergency_pin can be forcibly unpinned.
notable_tests: perf-lab soak (12h) with injected KV pressure showed ~32% fewer evacuations at peak and eliminated reopen oscillation in the canary window. Integration and e2e suites updated; one integration flake was a CI environment issue and rerun passed.
authors_notes: This is a hotpatch motivated by a live incident. Implemented as a conservative, opt-in mitigation set with observability and admin controls. Please coordinate with SRE on rollout timing (I will be oncall during canary).
